ai.description: Sharma’s Racer is a slender, medium-sized colubrid with a greyish-brown body and a distinct white stripe along the vertebral line. It features a dark post-ocular streak and smooth dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Platyceps bholanathi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, narrow dark stripe running through the eye, which is absent in other similar Indian racers.
ai.habitat: Platyceps bholanathi inhabits the rocky, arid, and semi-arid scrublands of central India, typically found at low to moderate elevations among boulders and dry vegetation.
ai.behavior: Sharma's Racer is a diurnal snake that actively hunts its prey, primarily lizards, by foraging across rocky terrains and scrublands during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: Platyceps bholanathi is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding activity typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Platyceps bholanathi is endemic to India, primarily inhabiting the rocky, arid landscapes of Rajasthan and Gujarat within the Thar Desert biogeographic zone.
